content.title: Outlier Impact on Measures of Center and Spread
content.overview: This lesson focuses on how extreme values, known as outliers, affect statistical measures. You will learn to distinguish between 'resistant' measures (like median and IQR) and 'sensitive' measures (like mean and range) when a data set contains a value significantly higher or lower than the rest.
learning_objectives: Identify outliers within a univariate data set.
Compare the sensitivity of the mean versus the robustness of the median when an outlier is introduced.
Analyze how outliers affect measures of spread, specifically comparing the range and the Interquartile Range (IQR).

sections.title: Defining Outliers and Sensitivity
sections.content:
An outlier is a data point that differs significantly from other observations in a data set. In statistics, we categorize measures based on how they react to these values. A 'sensitive' measure is one that changes substantially when an outlier is added or modified. A 'resistant' (or robust) measure is one that remains relatively stable despite the presence of extreme values.

![A flow chart showing which statistical measures are sensitive or resistant to outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/97bd8f31-7097-445a-9fd2-9e5f2900fe94-1786506131010-641.webp)

sections.title: Measures of Center: Mean vs. Median
sections.content: The mean (average) is highly sensitive to outliers because its calculation involves summing every value in the set. A single very large number will pull the mean upward, while a very small number will pull it downward. In contrast, the median is the middle value of an ordered list. Because it depends on position rather than the magnitude of every value, the median is resistant to outliers. If you change the largest value in a set to an even larger number, the middle position remains the same.

sections.title: Measures of Spread: Range vs. IQR
sections.content: The range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values. Since outliers are by definition extreme maximums or minimums, the range is extremely sensitive to them. The Interquartile Range (IQR) is the difference between the third quartile (Q3) and the first quartile (Q1). Because the IQR focuses on the middle 50% of the data, it ignores the extreme ends and is therefore resistant to outliers.

worked_examples.question: Original data set: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. If the value 11 is replaced with 100, how do the mean, median, range, and IQR change?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the outlier. 100 is much larger than the other values (5-10). Step 2: Compare the Mean. Original mean = (5+6+7+8+9+10+11)/7 = 8. New mean = (5+6+7+8+9+10+100)/7 ≈ 20.7. The mean increases significantly. Step 3: Compare the Median. Both sets have 7 values. The middle (4th) value in both ordered sets is 8. The median is unchanged. Step 4: Compare the Range. Original range = 11 - 5 = 6. New range = 100 - 5 = 95. The range increases significantly. Step 5: Compare the IQR. In both sets, Q1 is 6 and Q3 is 10. IQR = 10 - 6 = 4. The IQR is unchanged.

common_mistakes: Assuming the IQR always changes when the range changes. The IQR only changes if the outlier shifts the 25th or 75th percentile values.
Thinking the median is 'affected' just because the mean is. The median only shifts if the middle position's value changes.
Confusing 'spread' with 'center'. Range and IQR measure how far apart data is; mean and median measure the 'middle'.
exam_tips: If an ACT question asks which measure changes the LEAST when an outlier is added, look for Median or IQR in the choices.
If a question asks which measure is most affected by a 'suspect value,' look for Mean or Range.
You don't always need to calculate the exact new mean; if you see a huge outlier, you know the mean will move in that direction.
content.recap: Outliers pull the mean and range toward the extreme value. However, the median and IQR are resistant measures that typically remain stable because they rely on the relative positioning of the central data points rather than the values of the extremes.

knowledge_claims.content: An outlier is a data point that is significantly higher or lower than the rest of the values in a data set.
The mean is more sensitive to outliers than the median because the mean incorporates the specific value of every data point.
The median is a resistant measure of center because it is determined by the middle position of an ordered data set.
The range is highly sensitive to outliers because it is calculated using the maximum and minimum values.
The Interquartile Range (IQR) is resistant to outliers because it measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data (Q3 - Q1).
Adding a very large outlier to a data set will increase the mean while the median likely remains the same.
Adding a very small outlier to a data set will decrease the mean while the median likely remains the same.
To determine the impact of an outlier on the range, subtract the new minimum from the new maximum and compare it to the original difference.
If a data set's mean is significantly different from its median, it is a strong indicator that the data contains outliers or is skewed.
It is a mistake to assume that the IQR must increase whenever the range increases due to an outlier.
To verify if a measure is resistant, check if its calculation depends on the extreme values (min/max) or the central values (middle/quartiles).
In a set of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, replacing 25 with 500 will increase the mean and range but leave the median at 15.

items.stem:
Practice form 1.
Adding a very large outlier to a data set will usually affect which measure more?
A) the median
B) the mode in every case
C) the mean
D) the sample size only
items.explanation: The mean is more sensitive to extreme values.
